title: Which four digit palindromes does four divide?
description: A palindrome has the same first and last digit, and four divides a number when it divides its last two digits. The video uses both facts to find the largest and the smallest four digit palindromes that four divides.
teaching_notes: One idea: a four digit palindrome has the shape first, middle, middle, first, so the last two digits are the middle digit and the first digit, and the test for four decides which middle digit works. Watch for students who give nine thousand nine hundred and ninety nine or one thousand and one, which are odd.

video_script.why: The child uses the last two digits to test for four, fixes the first digit from the evenness of the last, and tries the middle digit from the top and from the bottom.
video_script.substitution: A four digit palindrome ends with its first digit, so try the biggest and the smallest even first digit, and choose the middle digit whose last two digits make a multiple of 4.
video_script.anchor: four boxes in a row for the four digits of a palindrome, with the first and last boxes joined by an arc
video_script.payoff_line: Largest, eight thousand eight hundred and eighty eight; smallest, two thousand one hundred and twelve

final_answer.spoken: the largest is eight thousand eight hundred and eighty eight, and the smallest is two thousand one hundred and twelve

maths_rules: a four digit palindrome has the shape abba, so its first and last digits are equal
4 divides only even numbers, so the last digit a is even; it is not 0 because the first digit cannot be 0, so a is 2, 4, 6 or 8
4 divides abba exactly when 4 divides the number made by its last two digits, 10b + a
largest: a = 8; b = 9 gives 98 = 24 x 4 + 2, which is not a multiple of 4; b = 8 gives 88 = 22 x 4, so 8888
smallest: a = 2; b = 0 gives 2, which is not a multiple of 4; b = 1 gives 12 = 3 x 4, so 2112
the larger palindrome 8998 is not divisible by 4, since 98 is not; 2002 is not either, since 2 is not
video_script.design: One idea: the palindrome shape fixes the first and last digits as equal and even, then the last two digits decide. Callback to the test on the last two digits. Wrong idea: none is broken. The four boxes stay on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, look at the first digit. The first and last digits of a palindrome are the same.
<bookmark mark='even'/>Four divides only even numbers, so the last digit is even.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The first digit cannot be zero in a number with four digits.
<bookmark mark='left'/>That leaves two, four, six or eight.

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>Step two, find the largest. Take the biggest first digit, which is eight.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Try nine in the middle. The last two digits make ninety eight.
<bookmark mark='ninesix'/>Four times twenty four is ninety six, so ninety eight leaves two over.
<bookmark mark='eighty'/>Try eight in the middle. The last two digits make eighty eight.
<bookmark mark='fours'/>That is twenty two fours, so the largest is eight thousand eight hundred and eighty eight.

<bookmark mark='fours'/>That is three fours, so the smallest is two thousand one hundred and twelve.
